legend: Differentiated CIN (HPV-negative after sequencing). An acanthotic atypical epithelial proliferation that was adjacent to a keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma harbouring a TP53 gene mutation. The rete ridges are elongated and branching. The atypical basal cell proliferation reveals individual mitoses. Parakeratosis is focally prominent.

p53 wildtype verrucous CIN (HPV-negative after sequencing). There is an exophytic intraepithelial proliferation with acanthosis, marked hyperkeratosis, and lack of the granular cell layer. There is only mild atypia in the basal cell layers.

p53 wildtype basaloid CIN (HPV-negative after sequencing). A and B. An atypical full-thickness lesion and p16ink4a negativity representing an HPV-independent CIN without associated invasive squamous cell carcinoma. C and D Please note the differences in thickness of basaloid CIN, both photographed at 10× magnification. All lesions lack koiloytosis.
